baseline: baseline3dgs-tandt-30000 (avg 23.36: truck 25.21, train 21.52), baseline3dgs-db-30000 (avg 29.28: drjohnson 28.76, playroom 29.80)
paper_targets: Table 1 averages: T&T 23.75 (paper 3DGS 23.77), DB 29.78 (paper 3DGS 29.81); criterion +-0.5 dB on the complete dataset averages; compare Delta vs our baseline to the paper's Delta vs 3DGS (~0).
post: after each run: tools/ssenv python -m ss_faster_gs.profile --run <run> --views 50 -> <run>/fastergs_profile.json (forward / backward / update ms, Faster-GS+FusedAdam vs gsplat+torch Adam vs gsplat+fused torch Adam on the final checkpoint, same GPU). Speed is secondary; quality is the primary criterion.
notes: Paper reports dataset averages only (no per-scene quality) -> cheapest complete averages: tandt (2) + db (2). First use JIT-builds the vendored CUDA backend (~75 s, cached in ~/.cache/torch_extensions; concurrent first builds may race - build once before launching, e.g. by ss-verify). Training wall time in the bench is contaminated by other users on the shared GPUs; use the profile json for speed ratios.
